report:
Fresh source review of crates.sage_test_harness.compile_tests.query_capture against current captured claim, six ordinary implementation entries, and the complete two-test set. No TODO or N/A entries are present. This refresh executes only review start/read/record and source inspection; relevant test execution is centralized by root, so this report does not claim a new test run.

Cold/fresh setup: CompileTest::prepare materializes each project, performs independent rustc checking, opens a new SageHost, and drains setup events before entering with_context. Host open waits for metadata-provider readiness, constructs new Database storage/logs via with_proxy_and_cfgs, and registers configuration and source inputs. It does not demand the fixture root semantic products; setup_root_module is first called by with_context after the drain. The database association supplies actual request events/dispositions and mem::take drain semantics. Thus capture starts after project/provider setup but before local discovery.

Covered work: with_context performs tracked root discovery; collect calls check_crate and reads accumulated signature diagnostics before draining events. check_crate recursively visits the selected local modules and supported symbols, requests function signatures and bodies regardless of marker presence, and freezes body observations. Selector processing occurs only after this checking. The symbols implementation resolves local identities and external def_path names during walk_expr; FrozenType::read resolves recursive type names into owned values before the drain. Neither name-reading path is hidden from the log. Type and symbol observations share this pre-drain collection, and the returned TypeRows contain frozen values rather than deferred semantic lookups.

End boundary and optional behavior: collect takes the inspection log before matching/rendering frozen diagnostics and observations. FrozenType formatting receives no database, symbol fields are owned strings, and the captured trace projection consumes owned events with no database access. run compares expectations only after prepare returns. This control-flow/data-ownership inspection establishes the rendering/comparison boundary in addition to the real trace tests; no boundary-injection test is claimed. Queries are emitted only when an optional query expectation is present; omission returns an empty query output. Warm/edit/point-demand behavior is explicitly outside this v1 claim.

Complete tests: cold_queries_are_stable_across_isolated_projects separately prepares identical fixtures, checks equal nonempty executed body traces and absence of temporary paths and IDs. cold_capture_includes_discovery_and_observation_reads_without_changing_bodies prepares a fixture with an external Ordering variant and an unselected private function twice, with and without a symbol selector. It asserts the correct external variant identity, equality of the actual traces, executed setup_root_module, signature, body and tcx::def_path operations, and exactly two executed bodies. These are visible assertions over real production results, not wrapper-only or annotation-only evidence. They would catch omitted cold discovery/signatures, lost name-reading work, or selector-limited body checking for the exercised scenario. Inspection of the marker-independent recursive checker supports the general policy beyond this fixture.

All six implementation associations are accounted for: driver establishes setup/demand boundary; db supplies fresh capture state and event drain; compile prepares and later compares; observe checks/freezes/drains/renders in that order; symbols and types freeze semantic names before capture ends. The additional trace dependency is captured through review read and inspected for owned-event-only projection. Current evidence adequately supports the complete claim. No source edits or outstanding concerns arose in this refresh.
